title: Rubik's Cube Guides
summary: Printable, picture-based guides for kids: Layer-by-Layer and CFOP. Every move is checked in a cube simulator.

title: LogiPlan
summary: Plan a factory layout and its in-plant logistics in the browser, then watch it run. Roads, stations, AGVs, forklifts, live simulation and KPIs.

title: Familien-Werkstatt
summary: Small interactive pages to explore with your kids, one per topic: moon phases, rainbows, magnets, the water cycle and more. In German.

title: Agent Rodeo
summary: Different AI coding agents get the same brief: build a 3D Lego city in the browser. Click through each attempt and compare.

title: RAGE-o-meter
summary: A Claude Code plugin that counts how often you scold your agents per session. The only AI benchmark you can trust.

title: Pusteblume
summary: A painted page about dandelions. Blow into your microphone and the seeds fly away. In German.

title: Farbpunkte
summary: Fast tapping game for 2 to 4 players on one screen. When your color shows up, tap it before anyone else. In German.

title: PhantomCast
summary: Projection mapping with any projector. Map videos onto walls or windows and line up the surfaces from your phone.

title: Argus
summary: Self-hosted scanner for your home network. Finds every device, flags risky ports and known CVEs, and tells you when something new shows up.

title: Wiki Graph
summary: Finds the shortest path between any two Wikipedia articles and draws the links as a graph you can explore.

title: Dalli-Klick
summary: The TV guessing game as a desktop app for parties. A picture hides under hexagon tiles, and the earlier you guess, the more points.

title: Claude Buddy
summary: A tiny OLED desk display that shows what Claude Code is doing, with a mascot that reacts live. hermes-buddy is the Hermes version.

title: Claude Monitor
summary: Live dashboard for every Claude Code session on your machine: prompts, tools, sub-agents, tokens and cost.

title: NoHello for Agents
summary: One-page guide: give your coding agent the whole request in the first message, not "hey, can you help me?"
